summary:
We built Tellura, an open-source climate intelligence workstation for NASA's "Be An Earth System Trend Detective" challenge. Most tools draw straight lines over satellite charts. This creates false alarms because extreme weather and natural cycles distort basic averages.

Tellura connects to 44 years of authentic NASA POWER and MERRA-2 observations. It uses proven non-parametric mathematics to test whether changes are real permanent trends or just temporary noise. Our engine pairs Mann-Kendall rank tests with Hamed-Rao autocorrelation corrections, Theil-Sen median slopes, and Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate control.

Tellura answers the challenge prompts directly. It spots what is changing, where it changes on a 2D map and 3D globe, and how fast. It also finds opposing regional contrasts, like inland warming versus coastal ocean buffering over the same years.

This matters because cities and water managers risk wasting millions on wrong decisions. Tellura gives students, planners, and scientists audit-proof answers in three clicks with zero code, zero synthetic data, and zero false alarms.
details:
What It Does and How It Works

Tellura is an open-science climate intelligence workstation that detects multi-decadal trends across 44 years (1981–2024) of authentic NASA Earth observations. It streams live monthly reanalysis data directly from the NASA Langley POWER API and MERRA-2 products without relying on black-box assumptions:

  • Non-Parametric Trend Testing: Computes rank-based Mann-Kendall statistics with Hamed-Rao modified variance corrections to strip out false trends caused by natural weather persistence.
  • Robust Rate Estimation: Calculates Theil-Sen median slopes and Gilbert 95% confidence intervals, resisting up to 29.3% extreme outlier anomalies.
  • Multiple Testing Control: Applies the Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate (FDR, q <= 0.05) across thousands of spatial grid cells to eliminate statistical flukes.
  • Regime Shift & Spatial Clustering: Identifies exact tipping points via Pettitt changepoint testing, computes Anselin Local Moran's I (LISA) spatial regimes (Hotspots, Coldspots, Spatial Outliers), and calculates Burrows climate velocity vectors (km/decade) alongside Archimedean Copula compound hazard return periods (heatwaves + drought).

What Benefits It Has

  • Eliminates False Alarms: Distinguishes genuine multi-decadal structural climate trends from single-year extreme weather flukes.
  • Sub-Second Execution: Delivers live NASA analysis in under 2 seconds, and cached spatial queries in under 15 milliseconds.
  • Open-Science Reproducibility: Evaluators can verify every calculation with a single click by downloading CF-1.8 NetCDF-4 grids, GeoJSON boundaries, LaTeX equations, or launching an auto-generated, runnable Google Colab Python notebook.
  • Adaptive Personas: Serves 3 distinct user tracks—curiosity-driven guided STEM investigations for students, decadal infrastructure risk analytics for municipal planners, and rigorous statistical batteries for peer reviewers.

What Is the Intended Impact

  • Municipal Infrastructure Planning: Equips civil engineers and water management authorities with statistically defensible 30-year risk projections for stormwater, zoning, and heat resilience.
  • Classroom STEM Education: Enables high school and university students to investigate climate mysteries in their own regions using a guided 3-step hypothesis builder.
  • Democratizing Earth Observation: Bridges the technical gap between raw satellite NetCDF datasets and actionable community decisions.

Tools and Technologies Used

  • Backend: Python 3.12, FastAPI, Uvicorn, NumPy 2, SciPy, xarray, NetCDF4, SQLite (WAL mode with HMAC-SHA256 cache signing), and SlowAPI rate limiting.
  • Frontend: React 19, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Zustand 5, Leaflet 1.9, Chart.js 4.5, and KaTeX for mathematical notation.
  • Planetary Engine: HTML5 Canvas with custom orthographic ray projection for interactive 3D globe visualization.
  • Acoustic Sonification: Web Audio API oscillator synthesis converting 40-year decadal temperature trajectories into audible sound frequencies for accessibility.

How It Is Creative

  • Acoustic Data Sonification: Converts multi-decadal climate slopes into dynamic audio pitches, allowing visually impaired users and students to hear the difference between stable and warming climates.
  • Curtain Comparison Slider: A split-screen interactive curtain comparing continuous trend slopes against spatial autocorrelation regimes side-by-side.
  • Opposing Contrasts Detector: Automatically discovers and highlights adjacent micro-regions experiencing diverging climate trends over identical time periods (e.g., inland heating vs. marine cooling).

Factors We Considered

  • Strict Zero-Synthetic Rule: All production calculations are strictly bound to verified NASA POWER and MERRA-2 observations (is_synthetic: false).
  • Satellite Instrument Discontinuities: The platform alerts users to sensor transitions in historical records (such as the 2000/2001 switch to CERES) so hardware upgrades are never misinterpreted as environmental shifts.
  • Deterministic AI Safety: AI models are strictly downstream and decoupled from numeric analysis. AI never computes or touches numbers; it only translates pre-computed SciPy statistics into clear explanations.
